review_notes: I read all of Full.lean and the simp-relevant parts of the files it depends on: Functor.lean (`stableTransposeFunctor_obj`, `stableTransposeFunctor_map`), StableMorphism.lean (`stableMap_quotient_map`, `stableMap_id`), Equivalence.lean (the `@[simp high]` inverse rule) and Faithful.lean. Full.lean declares no simp lemmas of its own. The one finding is about the simp rule `stableTransposeFunctor_map`, which the Full instance in this file has to work around. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour or loops. I judged `stableMap_quotient_map` correctly non-simp, because it quantifies over auxiliary squares that simp could not supply. The pairing of `stableTransposeFunctor_obj` and `stableTransposeFunctor_map` looks safe from loops, since the right-hand side of the map rule contains no `Functor.map`. The uncertainty is whether a defeq-typed restatement elaborates and is accepted by simp as I expect.

findings.problem: The simp lemma `stableTransposeFunctor_map` rewrites `(stableTransposeFunctor P).map f` into `eqToHom _ ≫ (homMk …).op ≫ eqToHom _`. The two objects are definitionally equal (`stableTransposeFunctor_obj` is proved by `rfl`), and the lemma itself is proved only by `id_comp`/`comp_id`. So the two `eqToHom` terms are pure noise. The equations they are built from, `(stableTransposeFunctor P).obj M = op …`, are not syntactically `X = X`, so `eqToHom_refl` should not discharge them. Simp therefore leaves them in the goal. This file has to work around that. It builds `h'` by conjugating `h` with `eqToHom`, so that it can state `heq` without them. It also uses `rw` instead of `simp`, then needs a trailing `simp [h']` to cancel the casts. The simp interface also needed a priority patch elsewhere: Equivalence.lean marks `stableTransposeFunctor_map_inverse` as `@[simp high]` with the comment 'Use recovery before the general simp rule expanding a stable transpose map'. That is a sign of competing rules caused by the eager expansion.
findings.proposed_change: Restate `stableTransposeFunctor_map` in Functor.lean without the `eqToHom`s: `(stableTransposeFunctor P).map f = (ObjectProperty.homMk (AuslanderReitenTranspose.stableMap … f.hom)).op`. This should be accepted because the two sides have defeq types, and the proof would be `rfl`. Keep it `@[simp]`, or drop `@[simp]` and use it by name. Then the Full proof needs no `h'`. It can take `h.unop.hom` directly. The goal after `rw`/`simp` is `(homMk f' ).op = h` up to `Quiver.Hom.unop_inj`, with no `eqToHom` cleanup. The Faithful proof's `← Category.assoc, cancel_mono, cancel_epi` step and the `high` priority in Equivalence.lean could be re-examined at the same time.
findings.benefit: Simp normal forms for `(stableTransposeFunctor P).map f` would no longer contain `eqToHom` casts. The Full and Faithful proofs would be shorter and more robust. The ad-hoc `@[simp high]` priority ordering between `stableTransposeFunctor_map_inverse` and `stableTransposeFunctor_map` would become less delicate. Users of `Functor.preimage` and `map_preimage` would get readable goals.

evidence.excerpt:
-- Use recovery before the general simp rule expanding a stable transpose map.
@[simp high]
simp only [stableTransposeFunctor_map, ← Category.assoc, cancel_mono, cancel_epi] at hfg
